document: OpenDataRemoval Privacy Platform — Security & Secrets Management Specification

threat_model.deployment_context: Ubuntu/Debian Linux home server on a private LAN. Services bound to LAN interface (0.0.0.0) until Cloudflare Tunnel attached.
realistic_threats: Unauthorised LAN access — another device on the home network attempting to access the dashboard
Brute-force login attempts against SSH or the dashboard login endpoint
Container escape — a compromised Playwright container attempting to reach internal services
Data exposure on disk — unencrypted PII readable if host storage is physically accessed
Secrets leak — .env file committed to version control or left world-readable
Stale sessions — long-lived JWT tokens exploited if a device is stolen
out_of_scope: Supply chain attacks on Docker images
Network-level MITM within the LAN (assumed trusted)

design_decisions.secret_backup: .env file at runtime + GPG-encrypted backup copy stored outside project directory
design_decisions.rotation: Manual rotation with documented per-secret procedures — DB_ENCRYPTION_KEY rotation requires special PII re-encryption sequence
design_decisions.backup_strategy: pg_dump for consistent DB backup + volume tar for n8n workflows and screenshots. All backups GPG-encrypted before storage.
design_decisions.host_hardening: Intermediate — UFW firewall rules, fail2ban for SSH and login endpoint, host hardening checklist

secrets_inventory.description: Complete catalogue of all secrets used by OpenDataRemoval with generation commands and rotation complexity

secrets.name: DB_ENCRYPTION_KEY
secrets.purpose: pgcrypto symmetric key for PII column encryption in identity schema
secrets.rotation_complexity: HIGH — requires re-encrypting all PII rows with new key. See rotation procedure.
secrets.if_compromised: All PII in identity schema is readable. Rotate immediately, audit access logs.

secrets.name: JWT_SECRET
secrets.purpose: HS256 signing key for dashboard authentication tokens
secrets.rotation_complexity: LOW — all active sessions invalidated immediately. Users must re-login.
secrets.if_compromised: Attacker can forge tokens. Rotate immediately — all sessions invalidated on rotation.

secrets.name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
secrets.rotation_complexity: MEDIUM — requires Docker Compose down, pg password update, DATABASE_URL update, Compose up.
secrets.if_compromised: Full DB read/write access including encrypted PII (but not decryptable without DB_ENCRYPTION_KEY).

secrets.name: REDIS_PASSWORD
secrets.purpose: Redis authentication for Celery task broker
secrets.rotation_complexity: LOW — update .env, restart redis + worker + beat + api containers.
secrets.if_compromised: Attacker can inject Celery tasks. Rotate immediately.

secrets.name: N8N_WEBHOOK_SECRET
secrets.purpose: HMAC-SHA256 signing key for n8n → API webhook authentication
secrets.rotation_complexity: LOW — update .env and n8n environment variable, restart api + n8n.
secrets.if_compromised: Attacker can inject arbitrary broker records into registry.

secrets.name: N8N_BASIC_AUTH_PASSWORD
secrets.if_compromised: Attacker can modify broker discovery workflows.

secrets.name: SMTP_PASSWORD
secrets.purpose: Mailgun SMTP authentication for outbound removal emails
secrets.generation: Generated by Mailgun — rotate in Mailgun dashboard
secrets.if_compromised: Attacker can send emails from removal address. Rotate in Mailgun immediately.

secrets.name: IMAP_PASSWORD
secrets.purpose: Mailgun IMAP authentication for inbound email polling
secrets.generation: Generated by Mailgun — rotate in Mailgun dashboard
secrets.if_compromised: Attacker can read broker response emails. Rotate in Mailgun immediately.

secrets.name: ADMIN_PASSWORD
secrets.generation: Strong passphrase — minimum 16 characters, stored as bcrypt hash in DB
secrets.rotation_complexity: LOW — use dashboard Settings page or scripts/rotate_admin_password.sh.
secrets.if_compromised: Full admin access to dashboard. Change immediately via settings.
secrets.storage: bcrypt hash in auth.users only — never in .env after initial setup

secrets.name: INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN
secrets.purpose: Shared secret for playwright → api internal calls (e.g. captcha flag updates)
secrets.if_compromised: Internal API manipulation from compromised playwright container.

secret_generation.description: Commands to generate all secrets for initial setup. Run these before filling in .env.
secret_generation.one_liner:
Generate all at once and print labelled:
for key in DB_ENCRYPTION_KEY JWT_SECRET POSTGRES_PASSWORD REDIS_PASSWORD N8N_WEBHOOK_SECRET INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN; do echo "$key=$(openssl rand -hex 32)"; done

file_permissions.rationale: Readable only by owner — prevents other OS users and world from reading secrets

gitignore.pre_commit_hook: Add to .git/hooks/pre-commit: if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -q '^.env$'; then echo 'ERROR: .env staged for commit'; exit 1; fi

encrypted_backup.description: GPG-symmetric encrypted backup of .env stored outside the project directory
encrypted_backup.storage_recommendation: Store ~/opendataremoval-secrets-backup.gpg on a separate encrypted USB drive or cloud storage (Bitwarden file attachment, encrypted cloud folder)

rotation_procedures.recommended_schedule: Review secrets every 90 days. Rotate any secret that may have been exposed immediately.
rotation_procedures.rotation_reminder: Add to crontab: 0 9 1 */3 * echo 'OpenDataRemoval: 90-day secrets review due' | mail -s 'OpenDataRemoval Security Reminder' {admin_email}

JWT_SECRET.impact: All active dashboard sessions immediately invalidated — all users must re-login
steps: 5. All users will be prompted to re-login on next request
1. Generate new password: openssl rand -base64 24 | tr -d '/+=' | head -c 32
2. docker compose stop api worker beat playwright mailwatcher n8n
3. docker compose exec db psql -U opendataremoval -c "ALTER USER opendataremoval PASSWORD 'NEW_PASSWORD';"
4. Update POSTGRES_PASSWORD and DATABASE_URL in .env with new password
5. docker compose start api worker beat playwright mailwatcher n8n
6. Verify: docker compose exec api python -c 'from sqlalchemy import create_engine; create_engine(os.environ[DATABASE_URL]).connect()'

DB_ENCRYPTION_KEY.impact: CRITICAL — all PII must be re-encrypted. System unavailable during rotation. Full backup required first.
DB_ENCRYPTION_KEY.pre_requisite: Full pg_dump backup must be completed and verified BEFORE starting
steps: 1. STOP ALL SERVICES: docker compose down
5. Start only the db container: docker compose up -d db
6. Run re-encryption migration script: docker compose run --rm -e OLD_KEY=$OLD_KEY -e NEW_KEY=$NEW_KEY api python scripts/reencrypt_pii.py
7. Script iterates all encrypted columns in identity schema, decrypts with OLD_KEY, re-encrypts with NEW_KEY
10. Verify PII is readable: docker compose run --rm api python scripts/verify_encryption.py

reencrypt_script_logic.process: For each row: SELECT pgp_sym_decrypt(col, OLD_KEY), UPDATE SET col = pgp_sym_encrypt(decrypted, NEW_KEY). Commit per table.
reencrypt_script_logic.rollback: If script fails mid-run: restore from backup taken in step 2

REDIS_PASSWORD.impact: Brief task queue interruption during restart
steps: 3. docker compose restart redis api worker beat

N8N_WEBHOOK_SECRET.impact: n8n webhook calls will fail until both api and n8n are restarted

backup_procedures.description: pg_dump for consistent DB backup + volume tar for n8n workflows and screenshots

full_backup.description: Complete backup of all OpenDataRemoval data. Run before any destructive operation.

steps.command: docker compose exec -T db pg_dump -U opendataremoval opendataremoval --format=custom --compress=9 > /var/backups/opendataremoval/$BACKUP_DATE/opendataremoval_db.pgdump
steps.description: Custom format compressed pg_dump — restorable with pg_restore

steps.command: docker run --rm -v opendataremoval_n8n_data:/data -v /var/backups/opendataremoval/$BACKUP_DATE:/backup alpine tar czf /backup/n8n_data.tar.gz /data
docker run --rm -v opendataremoval_screenshots:/data -v /var/backups/opendataremoval/$BACKUP_DATE:/backup alpine tar czf /backup/screenshots.tar.gz /data
steps.description: Evidence screenshots — optional, can be omitted if disk space constrained
Verify backup is readable without extracting

steps: 2. Decrypt backup: gpg --decrypt opendataremoval_backup_DATE.tar.gz.gpg | tar xz -C /tmp/opendataremoval_restore
3. Restore DB: docker compose up -d db; docker compose exec -T db pg_restore -U opendataremoval -d opendataremoval --clean /tmp/opendataremoval_restore/DATE/opendataremoval_db.pgdump
4. Restore n8n: docker run --rm -v opendataremoval_n8n_data:/data -v /tmp/opendataremoval_restore/DATE:/backup alpine tar xzf /backup/n8n_data.tar.gz -C /
5. Restore screenshots (optional): same pattern as n8n

backup_schedule.frequency: Daily at 01:00 — before the 02:00 scan run
backup_schedule.retention: Keep 7 daily + 4 weekly + 3 monthly backups. Implement with logrotate or backup rotation script.
backup_schedule.offsite: Recommended: copy encrypted backup to external USB or cloud storage weekly

backup_size_estimates.db_pgdump: 1-50 MB depending on scan history volume (compressed custom format)
backup_size_estimates.screenshots: 50 MB - 2 GB depending on SCREENSHOT_RETENTION_DAYS and broker count

jwt.storage: In-memory only on frontend — never localStorage or cookies
jwt.revocation: auth.sessions table — revoked_at checked on sensitive operations
jwt.jti_claim: Session UUID — enables per-session revocation without key rotation

password_hashing.never_store: Plain text passwords must never appear in logs, API responses, or environment variables after initial setup

pii_encryption.key_source: DB_ENCRYPTION_KEY environment variable — never stored in DB
pii_encryption.query_implication: Encrypted columns cannot be indexed or used in WHERE clauses directly. Queries fetch by profile_id then decrypt in application layer.
pii_encryption.key_not_in_db: If DB_ENCRYPTION_KEY is lost or changed without re-encryption, all PII becomes unreadable. Key backup is critical.

docker_networks.opendataremoval_net: internal: true — no internet egress for db, redis, beat containers
docker_networks.opendataremoval_egress: Standard bridge — only api, worker, playwright, mailwatcher, n8n have egress
docker_networks.principle: Minimum necessary egress — database and scheduler never initiate outbound connections

lan_exposure.bind_address: 0.0.0.0 by default. Change to 127.0.0.1 when Cloudflare Tunnel attached.
lan_exposure.not_exposed: PostgreSQL (5432), Redis (6379), Playwright (8001) — internal Docker network only

headers.Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000 (add when HTTPS via Cloudflare Tunnel)

audit_log_integrity.append_only_enforcement: No UPDATE or DELETE SQL ever issued against audit.audit_log from application code
audit_log_integrity.sqlalchemy_guard: Audit log model has no update() or delete() methods exposed. Insert only.
audit_log_integrity.postgres_rls_recommendation: Optional: CREATE POLICY audit_insert_only ON audit.audit_log FOR DELETE USING (false); CREATE POLICY audit_insert_only_update ON audit.audit_log FOR UPDATE USING (false);
audit_log_integrity.tamper_detection: Audit log rows have monotonically increasing created_at — gaps or out-of-order timestamps indicate tampering

host_hardening.description: Intermediate host-level hardening for Ubuntu/Debian home server

rules: sudo ufw allow from 192.168.0.0/16 to any port 3000 comment 'OpenDataRemoval Dashboard LAN'
sudo ufw allow from 192.168.0.0/16 to any port 8000 comment 'OpenDataRemoval API LAN'
sudo ufw allow from 192.168.0.0/16 to any port 5678 comment 'n8n UI LAN'
ufw_firewall.note: Adjust 192.168.0.0/16 to match your actual LAN subnet
ufw_firewall.cloudflare_tunnel_update: When tunnel is active and HOST_BIND_ADDRESS=127.0.0.1, the UFW LAN rules become irrelevant but leave in place for fallback

ssh_jail.config:
[sshd]
enabled = true
port = ssh
maxretry = 5
bantime = 3600
findtime = 600

opendataremoval_login_jail.config:
[opendataremoval-login]
enabled = true
port = 8000
filter = opendataremoval-login
logpath = /var/log/docker/opendataremoval_api.log
maxretry = 10
bantime = 1800
findtime = 300

os_updates.action: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y
os_updates.frequency: Weekly. Enable unattended-upgrades for security patches: sudo apt install unattended-upgrades

docker_user.action: Run Docker as a non-root deploy user: sudo usermod -aG docker {deploy_user}
docker_user.note: Never run docker compose as root

docker_socket.action: Ensure /var/run/docker.sock is not mounted into any OpenDataRemoval container
docker_socket.verify: grep -r docker.sock docker-compose.yml — should return nothing

unnecessary_services.action: sudo systemctl disable --now {service} for any unused services

automatic_security_updates.action: sudo dpkg-reconfigure -plow unattended-upgrades — enable security updates only

log_rotation.action: Verify /etc/logrotate.d/ has entries for docker and system logs
log_rotation.opendataremoval_docker_logs: Docker json-file driver handles rotation via max-size/max-file in docker-compose.yml

security_verification_checklist.description: Run these checks after initial setup and after any configuration change

checks.command: for i in {1..12}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"x","password":"x"}'; done
